recent_signals.summary: Whisper-base ASR (captured 2026-09-19): From Adriatic promenade (ASR 'Aosto'), Zeihan maps spice-trade geopolitics as baseline for post-globalization trade. Pre-~1450: land/coastal micro-economies; East/SE Asian spices/silks/porcelains passed dozens–hundreds of middlemen via Central Asia → Ottoman Istanbul → coastal ship to Italian city-states (Venice, Genoa, Amalfi, Pisa) who 'made mad money' as Western Europe gateway, partnering with Islamic Turkey. Portuguese deep-water navigation (da Gama around Africa to India) cut out middlemen over centuries → Istanbul + Italian city-states went from wealthiest to cut off from primary funds. Today: 'technologies of globalization are failing'; deep-water nav stays but no country can protect sea lanes globally — US most powerful at intervening, none can protect → trade regionalizes/localizes and must militarize (shipping-company culture + Navy/military roles change). Single biggest impact: collapse of multi-step manufactured-goods / supply-chain trade (parts shoot back-and-forth thousands of times); goods that can't be produced locally or inside a network like the EU 'simply aren't going to be produced at all.' Baseline for economy in 5–10–15 years: 12th–14th century spice-trade / Adriatic sequestered-trade model. No equity tickers called.
themes: spice trade / Adriatic model as post-globalization baseline

recent_signals.title: Project Vault Doesn't Solve the Mineral Problem || Peter Zeihan
recent_signals.summary: Whisper-base ASR (captured 2026-09-19): Patreon Q on Project Vault — Trump-admin Feb program, ~$2bn to buy rare materials/rare earths (and broader criticals) via mining tailings and build a US stockpile. Zeihan is 'kind of glad this happened' / 'baby step in the right direction' but says it 'hardly doesn't deal with the core problem.' Digital-age materials (rare earths, gallium) are byproducts of other processing (e.g. silver-mine waste → rare earths; aluminum smelting → gallium). Concentrating feedstock in the US is only step one and 'not even the smart step'; smart step is build processing — ~70% of critical-materials processing is in China; US is effectively buying waste from Chinese processing and bringing it here. If China cuts off supply / disruption, US must build processing anyway or ship tailings back to China. Even finished-product / refined-metals reserves 'doesn't really take us too far' until processing exists. Raw-material sourcing is easy (Vault 'already filling up' / ASR 'project fault'). China-free system needs diplomacy with three robust mining sectors: Canada (stop '51st state'), Australia (stop 'not racist enough' rhetoric), Brazil (relations 'worst since at least the 1970s'). Without that diplomacy, rest is a 'rounding error' that continues Chinese dependence. No equity tickers called.
